messages:
Anna: Picking up the ingress multiplexing idea from RFC v2. I prototyped a lightweight multiplexer that keeps a short-lived "subscription ledger" for identical streaming reads. Wanted quick feedback on lifecycle edges: snapshot vs live delivery, stall detection, and how retries/hedges should interact.

Ben: Nice. Summary reaction: multiplexing is promising but we must preserve per-client semantics. Two high-level modes: (1) snapshot-multiplex: compute response once and replay to new subscribers (good for short-lived responses), (2) live-subscribe: join an in-flight stream and forward bytes as they arrive. Snapshot is simpler for billing and offsets; live-subscribe saves work but complicates offsets/cancels.

Chloe: We should default to live-subscribe for small dedupe windows (<=500ms) to minimize duplicate upstream work. Enforce explicit opt-in header `X-Multiplex: live` or `X-Multiplex: snapshot`. Deny for requests with side-effects or streaming-in payloads.

Devon: Key lifecycle gotcha: subscribers with different client-side timeouts. We cannot rewind the upstream; so each subscriber gets a subscription cursor. If a late subscriber arrives mid-stream, they can either start at current head (best-effort) or be redirected to snapshot fallback. I prefer head-join only if a join-safety predicate passes (no strict token accounting required).

Ben: For stall detection, use a hybrid: (a) detection window = 150ms no-progress for token stream, (b) soft-reconnect attempt once, (c) if repeated or backpressure_score high, schedule hedging. Score increments per stall and decays exponentially. This avoids immediate hedging on transient GC/queue hiccups.

Ellen: On hedging semantics: hedges must carry the multiplex fingerprint token so the multiplexer can decide winner and abort losers. But watch out: if winners are the cheapest model variants often, we may bias selection. Suggest prefer same-model replicas first, then cheap fallbacks.

Chloe: Memory/connection cost: with live-subscribe we maintain downstream connections and subscriber state. Limit subscribers per fingerprint to M (configurable, default 8). When subscriber count >= M, new subscribers should be sent to a fallback route (cheaper model or new upstream request) to avoid unbounded growth.

Devon: Billing attribution: approximate tokens-per-subscriber by observing byte/segment receipts and time of unsubscribe. Heuristic: attribute tokens up to last emitted token before unsubscribe; for late joiners, charge only tokens received after join. Document clearly in billing docs.

Anna: Observability: each multiplex group gets a root trace_id (X-Trace-Root) and every subscriber gets a child span with join/leave events. Emit metrics: active_subscribers, avg_subscriber_lifetime, cancelled_before_first_token, stalls_per_min, hedges_triggered.

Ben: Implementation sketch:
- fingerprint := sha256(normalized-prompt + model + params-sig)
- ledger map: fingerprint -> {upstream_handle, subscribers[], score, created_at, last_progress_at}
- join flow: check ledger, run join-safety (no side-effects, prompt-normalization match, subscriber_count < M), attach subscriber or route fallback
- progress tick: update last_progress_at on token arrival, if now-last_progress > detect_window -> increment score and run hedging logic
- winner election: first completed upstream wins; cancel others gracefully

Chloe: Non-goals: no multiplexing for requests that post-side-effects (e.g., db writes), no attempt to merge slightly-different prompts, no long-lived fanout beyond TTL (we're optimizing for bursty duplicate reads).

Devon: Edge-case: client requests with differing `max_tokens` values. We cannot safely reuse a single stream unless max_tokens are equal. Two choices: disallow join if max_tokens differ, or allow join but upstream always respects max(max_tokens) and subscribers with smaller budgets are cut off locally (but that causes divergent outputs). I vote disallow.

Ellen: Testing matrix: mixed-deadline joins, subscriber churn with high-frequency joins, hedging under simulated upstream stalls, billing delta tests (approx vs actual). Also load test with fallback routing when subscriber cap reached.

Anna: Config for prototype: opt-in header `X-Multiplex: live`, dedupe TTL 300ms, join-safety requires exact param fingerprint, subscriber cap M=6, stall_detect_ms=150, base_hedge_delay=80ms + jitter, score_decay_half_life=1min. We'll gate behind FF `edge.multiplexing.v1`.

deploy-bot: feature flag `edge.multiplexing.v1` toggled ON for staging by @Anna  5 hosts. Logs -> #eng-sre.

Ben: I'll write RFC follow-up focusing on microbench results and failure modes, and propose a metric set for SLO alerts (hedge-rate, cancellation-rate, subscriber-reuse efficiency).

Chloe: +1. Also add a developer debug header `X-Multiplex-Debug: trace` that returns join timestamps and upstream id for the subscriber (opt-in only).

Devon: I'll take the prototype pairing with Anna this week to wire tracing + cancel semantics. Let's keep the initial rollout conservative.

Anna: Thanks everyone. I'll open the prototype PR and include a short README with non-goals and operator runbook for resetting stuck ledgers. Follow-ups: Ben RFC, Ellen test plan, Chloe doc changes.
